'''Jeb F. Willenbring''' is a [[Professor|Full Professor]] and Associate Chair for Graduate Mathematics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee|University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jeb Willenbring|url=https://uwm.edu/math/people/willenbring-jeb/|website=University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee}}</ref> Most of his research falls within the categories of [[Representation theory|Representation Theory]], [[Discrete mathematics|Discrete Mathematics]], and [[Mathematical physics|Mathematical Physics]]. His current research consists of several collaborations concerning [[algebraic combinatorics]] and various aspects of Representation Theory. Willenbring has published multiple papers concerning the nature of [[Littlewood-Richardson coefficient|Littlewood-Richardson coefficients]], a particular focus of his, in collaboration with Professors [[Pamela E. Harris|Pamela Harris]], Mark Colorusso, and William Erickson.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://sites.uwm.edu/jw/research/|website=UWM}}</ref>

== Education/Academic Career ==
Willenbring attended [[North Dakota State University]] during his undergraduate years and graduated with a bachelor's degree in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeb Willenbring |url=https://uwm.edu/math/people/willenbring-jeb/ |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=Mathematical Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref> After graduating, he went on to pursue a PhD degree in mathematics from the [[University of California, San Diego]]. He worked with his doctoral advisor, [[Nolan Wallach|Nolan Russell Wallach]], to produce his thesis ''Stability Properties for q-Mulitplicities and Branching Formulas for Representations of the Classical Groups''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jeb Faulkner Willenbring|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=44400|website=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref>

After receiving his PhD in mathematics in 2000, he accepted an Assistant Professor position at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee|University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee]] in 2003. He was promoted to an Associate Professor position in 2008 and to a Full Professor position in 2013. During his time at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee|University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee]], Willenbring has taught numerous classes including Advanced Calculus, Number Theory, and Graduate Algebra and supervised 9 Graduate Student theses to the point of completion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research {{!}} Jeb Willenbring |url=https://sites.uwm.edu/jw/research/ |access-date=2022-10-10 |language=en-US}}</ref> As a legally blind professor, he is a particularly zealous advocate for students with disabilities.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Quirk|first=Kathy|date=September 18, 2020|title=App will help visually impaired UWM students and visitors navigate campuses|url=https://uwm.edu/news/app-will-help-visually-impaired-uwm-students-and-visitors-navigate-campuses/}}</ref> As a member of his university's ADA advisory committee, Willenbring successfully advocated to bring an app for visually impaired student to campus,<ref>{{Cite web |last=desantsa@uwm.edu |date=2021-01-15 |title=Professor Jeb Willenbring Featured for Bringing App for the Blind and Visually Impaired to UWM |url=https://uwm.edu/math/professor-jeb-willenbring-featured-for-bringing-app-for-the-blind-and-visually-impaired-to-uwm/ |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=Mathematical Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref> making UWM the first university in its state to offer a free app for the blind and visually impaired.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UWM becomes 1st university in state to offer app for blind and visually impaired |url=https://www.cbs58.com/news/uwm-becomes-1st-university-in-state-to-offer-app-for-blind-and-visually-impaired |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=CBS58 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Milwaukee |first=Urban |title=UWM is first university in state to offer Aira app for blind and visually impaired |url=https://urbanmilwaukee.com/pressrelease/uwm-is-first-university-in-state-to-offer-aira-app-for-blind-and-visually-impaired/ |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=Urban Milwaukee == Awards ==
Willenbring has received numerous awards and grants. After graduating from his PhD Program, he taught at [[Yale University]] from 2000–2003 and was granted NSF VIGRE funding.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Willenbring |first=Jeb |date=2002 |title=An application of the Littlewood restriction formula to the Kostant-Rallis Theorem |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=354 |issue=11 |pages=4393–4419 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-02-03065-9 |doi-access=free |issn=0002-9947}}</ref> In 2013, Willenbring was named as a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society|American Mathematics Society]] as part of its inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#j |access-date=2022-10-11 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> Recognizing his work towards increasing campus accessibility, Willenbring also received a UWM Accessibility Resource Center Excellence Award in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2016-05-02 |title=Accessibility Resource Center Excellence Award winners |url=https://uwm.edu/news/accessibility-resource-center-excellence-award-winners/ |access-date=2022-10-11 |website=UWM REPORT |language=en-US}}</ref>
